chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — it reached him that
women, one of them would call for a lantern in the depths of the night to examine whether the menstrual blood had ceased; so he would censure this and say: 'When have women ever done this?'

key_terms.الطُّهْر: Purity; specifically the cessation of menstrual blood discharge, marking the return to ritual purity
key_terms.الْمِصْبَاح: Lantern or lamp; an oil lamp used for illumination in classical times
key_terms.جَوْف اللَّيْل: The depths/middle of the night; typically referring to the darkest part of the night
key_terms.يَعِيب: To censure, find fault with, consider blameworthy; the Imam's condemnation of this practice

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about using a lamp to check for the end of menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Baqir's (peace be upon him) disapproval of women using lanterns in the middle of the night to examine whether their menstruation had ended. His rhetorical question 'When did women ever do this?' implies that the established practice was checking with a piece of cotton (al-kursuf), without the need for artificial light. This ruling pertains to the method of istibraa' — checking whether a menstruating woman has achieved tahara (ritual purity). The Imam's tone indicates that resorting to special instruments or lights contradicts the established Sunnah for determining the end of menstruation.
